title: Vulnerable seroval 1.6.9 resolved into the runtime SSR/hydration dependency chain
description: pnpm audit reports two advisories against seroval@1.6.9: GHSA-f86p-h4j2-7qgj (code injection via a typed array's own constructor property, vulnerable >=1.6.0 <1.6.11) and GHSA-9wx9-5pv9-3349 (script injection via unescaped '<' in RegExp sources, vulnerable >=1.5.5 <1.6.10). pnpm why seroval shows exactly one deduped install (1.6.9) shared by @tanstack/router-core, which is pulled in by @tanstack/react-start (a direct runtime dependency of this theme, used for every SSR request's loader-data serialization/hydration) as well as by @tanstack/react-start-server, @tanstack/start-server-core and @tanstack/start-client-core. The devDependency path pnpm audit happens to print (via @tanstack/router-plugin) does not make this build-time-only: because only one seroval install exists in the whole tree, the same vulnerable version is the one actually loaded at request-serving time by the genuinely runtime start packages.
root_cause: node_modules/@tanstack/router-core/package.json declares "seroval": "^1.6.7" and pnpm-lock.yaml has resolved the single deduped seroval install for the whole tree to 1.6.9, a version inside both GHSA vulnerable ranges. ^1.6.7 already permits versions up to <2.0.0, so this is a stale lockfile resolution, not a semver ceiling imposed by the dependent package.
intended_behavior: The serialization layer used for every SSR response (loader-data dehydration embedded in the server-rendered HTML for client hydration) should not contain a known code/script-injection flaw in its typed-array or RegExp serialization paths.

trace.description: @tanstack/react-start is a direct runtime dependency (not devDependency) of this theme -- TanStack Start's server-rendering/hydration-data-serialization package, invoked on every SSR request.

@tanstack/router-core (pulled in transitively by @tanstack/react-start and the other runtime start-* packages, confirmed deduped to a single instance via pnpm why seroval) declares "seroval": "^1.6.7", a range that already permits the patched 1.6.11+ releases.

The lockfile has resolved and pinned the single deduped seroval install for the entire tree to 1.6.9 -- inside both advisory vulnerable ranges -- which is the version actually loaded at runtime by router-core's serialization code during SSR.

evidence.description: "@tanstack/react-start": "~1.168.57" listed under top-level dependencies, confirming it ships to production/runtime, not build-tooling only.

seroval@1.6.9: {} -- the single resolved/installed version for the whole repo; independently confirmed via pnpm audit --json (advisories 1243609 and 1243611, both reporting finding version 1.6.9) and pnpm why seroval ("Found 1 version of seroval").
"seroval": "^1.6.7" -- the declared range already permits patched versions (1.6.10, 1.6.11, and current latest 1.8.1), so the fix requires only a lockfile/version bump, not a package.json override.

conditions.description: Exploitability depends on seroval's own internal behavior, not on this theme's application code: GHSA-f86p-h4j2-7qgj requires a typed array with an attacker-influenced own constructor property to reach serialize/crossSerialize/Serializer; GHSA-9wx9-5pv9-3349 requires a RegExp built from untrusted pattern syntax containing '<' to be serialized and embedded in a <script> element. Whether this theme's own route loaders construct typed arrays or RegExps from attacker-controlled input and pass them through loader data was not found in this repo's source; that precondition belongs to the framework/application layer generally, not something independently established here.

execution.attacker_perspective: An attacker cannot trigger this directly against theplayroom.sa without first finding an application code path (in this theme or in the TanStack Start/Router framework itself) that serializes, via seroval, either (a) a typed array whose own constructor property has been set from attacker-controlled data, or (b) a RegExp built from an attacker-controlled pattern string containing '<'. If loader data containing such a value were dehydrated into the SSR HTML response, the injected constructor name or unescaped RegExp source would be written verbatim into the serialized JS embedded in a <script> tag, running attacker script in every visitor's browser on that page.
payloads: A typed array (e.g. Uint8Array) with an own enumerable constructor property reassigned to a malicious value, serialized by serialize/crossSerialize/Serializer/compileJSON (GHSA-f86p-h4j2-7qgj).
A RegExp constructed from untrusted pattern text containing '<', serialized and embedded inside an HTML <script> element during SSR (GHSA-9wx9-5pv9-3349).
instructions: Run `pnpm audit --json` at the repo root and confirm advisories 1243609 (GHSA-f86p-h4j2-7qgj) and 1243611 (GHSA-9wx9-5pv9-3349) are present with module_name seroval, version 1.6.9.
Run `pnpm why seroval` and confirm a single resolved version (1.6.9) shared by @tanstack/router-core and, through it, by @tanstack/react-start and the other start-* runtime packages.
After remediation, re-run `pnpm audit --json` and confirm seroval no longer appears in the advisories list, and `pnpm why seroval` reports a version >= 1.6.11.
execution.observed_result: Installed/resolved version seroval@1.6.9 (pnpm-lock.yaml:6548), confirmed by pnpm audit --json (both advisories report finding version 1.6.9) and pnpm why seroval (exactly one deduped install). 1.6.9 falls inside both vulnerable ranges. @tanstack/router-core (package.json:171) declares seroval "^1.6.7", which already permits patched releases (latest published is 1.8.1).

remediation.strategy: Lockfile-resolution fix, not a package.json range change: @tanstack/router-core's own declared range (^1.6.7) already permits the patched seroval releases (>=1.6.11), so no pnpm.overrides/package.json pinning is required. Run `pnpm update seroval` to let pnpm re-resolve the single deduped seroval install to a version >= 1.6.11, commit the updated pnpm-lock.yaml, then re-run pnpm build/typecheck/test and pnpm audit to confirm the advisories are gone.

code_changes.fixed_code: (generated by `pnpm update seroval` -- bumps the single deduped seroval entry from 1.6.9 to >=1.6.11 within the existing ^1.6.7 range already declared by @tanstack/router-core; no package.json edit needed)

likelihood.reason: Both advisories require a narrow precondition (an attacker able to inject an own constructor property onto a serialized typed array, or an attacker-controlled RegExp pattern containing '<' reaching serialization) that was not found to exist in this theme's own route/loader code; the precondition lives in the shared framework dependency, not demonstrated application-reachable input in this repo.

impact.reason: If the precondition is met, the result is script injection into the server-rendered HTML sent to every visitor of the affected page, since seroval's serialization runs on SSR responses for hydration across this TanStack Start app -- consistent with the advisories' own moderate CVSS ratings.

confidence.reason: The installed version, its membership in both vulnerable ranges, runtime (not build-only) reachability via @tanstack/react-start's dependency tree, and the fact that the dependent's declared semver range already permits a patched version were independently reproduced from this repo's own pnpm audit --json output, pnpm why seroval, pnpm-lock.yaml, and the installed router-core package.json by a fresh verifier agent, not inferred from the original candidate alone.

title: Theme's public/_headers sets Cache-Control only; no baseline security response headers declared for any path
description: public/_headers is the only file in this repository through which the theme itself can declare static response headers (Cloudflare-Pages-style _headers syntax). Its entire content is a single rule scoping Cache-Control to /assets/*. No rule exists for X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options / Content-Security-Policy frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, or Strict-Transport-Security, for /assets/* or any other path including /* (the whole site). A repo-wide search of every theme-owned server-rendering entry point (app/server.ts, app/start.ts, vite.config.ts, app/routes/__root.tsx, and every file under app/routes) found no middleware, route-level headers() export, or response.setHeader call that sets any of these headers either.
root_cause: The theme ships only a cache-control rule in public/_headers and never adds a catch-all (/*) security-header rule, and no custom TanStack Start middleware or root-route headers() export was added to compensate. The gap is an omission: nothing actively removes or overrides headers, it simply never declares the recommended baseline ones.
intended_behavior: A production storefront should serve, for every response the theme's own layer influences, baseline hardening headers (X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, a frame-ancestors/X-Frame-Options restriction, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, and Strict-Transport-Security over HTTPS) regardless of what the hosting edge separately does, since defense-in-depth at the theme layer costs nothing and is the only layer this repository's own source can attest to.

trace.description: The only rule declared is scoped to /assets/* (Cache-Control); no catch-all (/*) rule exists for any security header.
export default withThemeSentry(handler, 'raed') -- the entire file is 4 lines wrapping the TanStack Start server-entry handler with Sentry; no header-setting logic of any kind.

Grep for 'headers()', 'X-Frame-Options', 'Content-Security-Policy', 'Strict-Transport-Security', 'Referrer-Policy', 'Permissions-Policy', 'X-Content-Type-Options' across app/routes and vite.config.ts returned no matches; every HTTP response this theme's own layer influences is sent without any of these five headers unless added by a layer outside this repository.

evidence.description: /assets/*\n  Cache-Control: public, max-age=31556952, immutable -- the file's entire content.

import { withThemeSentry } from '@salla.sa/twilight-theme-engine/sentry/server'; import handler from '@tanstack/react-start/server-entry'; export default withThemeSentry(handler, 'raed'); -- no header-setting code.

conditions.description: Applies to the theme's own build/source layer only; whether theplayroom.sa's actual served responses are additionally protected depends on Salla's production hosting edge configuration, which is outside this repository and not something its source can confirm or deny (platform-level settings are an owner review item per this project's AGENTS.md).

execution.attacker_perspective: The risk is the absence of theme-layer defense-in-depth against clickjacking (framing the storefront in a malicious iframe to overlay fake UI/phishing), MIME-sniffing-based content-type confusion, referrer leakage of URLs to third-party resources, and (if HSTS is absent end-to-end) downgrade/SSL-stripping on first visit. All are mitigated by the headers listed, none of which this repo's source adds.
payloads: N/A -- this is a configuration/omission gap, not an injectable payload
instructions: Once a public or staging URL for this theme build exists, run `curl -I https://<staging-or-prod-url>/` and inspect the response headers for X-Frame-Options / Content-Security-Policy, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, and Strict-Transport-Security.
Separately run `curl -I https://<url>/assets/<some-asset>` to confirm only Cache-Control is present there, matching this repo's _headers file.

If any of the five headers already appear on the live response despite this repo's _headers not declaring them, Salla's hosting edge is adding them independently of this repository, which lowers real-world impact accordingly without changing whether this repo's own layer should still add them.
execution.observed_result: public/_headers and the build output dist/client/_headers both contain only the Cache-Control rule for /assets/*. Grep across app/server.ts, app/start.ts, vite.config.ts, app/routes/__root.tsx, and all files under app/routes found zero occurrences of any of the five target header names or of a TanStack Start route-level headers() export.

remediation.strategy: Add a catch-all security-header rule to the theme-owned public/_headers file so every response this theme's static-hosting layer serves carries the standard baseline headers, independent of whatever Salla's platform edge may or may not already set. This is a no-cost, strictly beneficial change: it cannot be redundant-harmful, and it closes the repo's own-layer gap regardless of the unresolved platform-edge fact. The existing /assets/* Cache-Control rule is unrelated and stays as-is.

code_changes.fixed_code:
/*
  X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
  Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin
  Permissions-Policy: camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=()
  Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains; preload

/assets/*
  Cache-Control: public, max-age=31556952, immutable

likelihood.reason: Exploiting the absence of these headers requires a separate attack vector (e.g. an attacker-controlled page framing theplayroom.sa, or a MIME-confusion payload) layered on top of the missing header, not a direct exploit of the gap itself, and the platform edge may already supply some or all of these headers independent of this repo.

impact.reason: If genuinely unprotected end-to-end, the realistic impact is clickjacking/UI-redress and minor referrer information leakage against a single-merchant storefront with no admin/auth surface exposed here -- not data exfiltration or RCE. Severity is calibrated to what is demonstrated (this repo's own layer contributes nothing), not to an unverified worst case.

confidence.reason: The file content, the identical post-build output, and the absence of any header-setting code across every theme-owned server/route/config file were all verified directly from source by a fresh, independent verifier agent, not inferred from the original candidate alone. The only residual uncertainty (platform-edge behavior) is explicitly out of scope for a source-only confirmation and does not affect confidence in the repo-layer finding itself.

title: resolveLink.ts passes the engine-resolved CTA target string into an href with no scheme check of its own
description: app/lib/resolveLink.ts returns a home-block CTA link-target string unchanged (trimmed, with '#' and empty treated as absent) for direct use as an href across several home blocks. The string originates from the Salla dashboard's own link-target picker field, resolved server-side by the engine before this theme's code ever sees it. Whether that dashboard picker UI constrains the merchant to http(s)/relative targets, or would accept and resolve freehand text containing a javascript: scheme, is not visible from this repository's source.
claimed_root_cause: If the engine's dashboard link-picker allows a merchant to enter or resolve to a javascript:-scheme (or other executable-scheme) string, and resolveLink.ts performs no scheme allowlist of its own before that string is used as an href, a merchant (or anyone with dashboard access) could set a self-XSS-capable link. Per this audit's trust calibration, a merchant acting against their own storefront is self-impact, not a crossed boundary -- but the decisive fact (does the picker actually constrain schemes) is not source-visible, so this cannot be confirmed or rejected from this repository alone.

trace.description: Accepts the engine-resolved CTA target string and returns it trimmed, with only '#' and empty excluded -- no scheme or protocol check of any kind.
The unmodified string is returned for direct use as an href by the calling home-block component.

evidence.description: export function resolveLink(value: unknown): string | undefined { if (typeof value !== 'string') return undefined; const trimmed = value.trim(); return trimmed && trimmed !== '#' ? trimmed : undefined; }

blockers: The Salla dashboard's link-target picker UI and its server-side resolution logic are not present in this repository's source, so whether the resolved string is constrained to safe schemes (http/https/relative paths) cannot be established from here.

validation_plan.local: Not resolvable locally: the picker UI and its resolution logic live in the Salla dashboard/engine backend, not in this repository.
validation_plan.deployment: On the Stage 14 staging store, have the owner attempt to set a home-block CTA link-target field to a javascript: URI (or confirm the picker UI only offers page/product/category selection plus a URL field that itself validates http(s)) and observe whether the dashboard accepts and resolves it. If the picker only accepts http(s)/relative targets by construction, this is rejected with no code change needed; if it accepts freehand javascript: text, add a scheme allowlist to resolveLink.ts (reject any scheme other than http:, https:, or a relative path) as the smallest fix.
